title: Pixels to Keys: Exploring Spatial and Motion Cues in Gameplay Inverse Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2609.37907v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Video games offer scalable environments for studying perception and control in embodied agents.Abundant online gameplay videos could supply demonstrations, but they rarely include player inputs for training. Inverse Dynamics Models (IDMs) have thus been proposed to infer inputs from frames. Large (up to 1B parameters) IDMs trained on $\sim$1K-2K gameplay hours demonstrate feasibility and cross-environment generalization at this scale, but researchers do not clarify what the key components are to recover individual actions and often report only aggregate accuracy that can mask rare-action failures. We study the problem in a data-constrained scenario to evaluate how spatial motion features, model architectures, and training objectives affect an IDM's outcome and we analyse our models on per-key and balanced metrics such as $F_1^{macro}$. translated_title: 从像素到按键：探索游戏逆动力学中的空间与运动线索
translated_abstract: 电子游戏为研究具身智能体的感知与控制提供了可扩展的环境。丰富的在线游戏视频本可以提供示范数据，但这些视频很少包含用于训练的玩家输入信息。因此，研究者提出了逆动力学模型（IDMs），用于从视频帧中推断玩家输入。在约1000-2000小时游戏数据上训练的大型IDM（高达10亿参数）已经证明了该方法的可行性以及在此规模下的跨环境泛化能力，但现有研究并未阐明恢复单个按键动作所需的关键组件，且通常仅报告总体准确率，这可能掩盖模型在稀有按键上的失败。我们在数据受限的场景中研究这一问题，以评估空间运动特征、模型架构和训练目标如何影响IDM的表现，并使用逐按键的平衡指标（如宏平均F1）对模型进行分析。我们在Trackmania游戏上的实验突出了模型架构和运动特征等因素的重要性。
tldr: 该论文在数据受限场景下系统研究了空间运动特征、模型架构与训练目标对游戏逆动力学模型的影响，并采用宏平均F1等平衡指标进行逐按键评估，揭示了影响单个按键动作恢复的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates how spatial and motion features, model architectures, and training objectives affect Inverse Dynamics Models for gameplay in a data-constrained setting, using balanced per-key metrics like macro-F1 to identify the key factors for recovering individual player actions.
